```{r setup}
library("ggplot2")
library("ggpattern")
```

## Overview

`{ggpattern}` provides a pattern version of most `{ggplot2}` geoms (e.g. `geom_rect_pattern()`).
For any other geom (from `{ggplot2}` or an extension package) there are three ways to fill its areas with patterns,
from the least to the most work:

1. `with_pattern()` makes a pattern layer from a layer, for a one-off plot.
2. `make_GeomPattern()` makes a pattern geom from a geom, for a reusable `geom_*_pattern()` function.
3. Writing the pattern geom's draw methods yourself with `with_pattern_aes()` and `with_pattern_key()`,
   for full control.

All three draw the parent geom's grob as usual and then fill each of its areas
with the pattern of its row of the layer's data using `gridpattern::with_pattern()`.
Each area's fill, pattern, and border are drawn in turn (like `{ggplot2}` draws its areas)
so overlapping areas stack as they would without patterns.

To write a new *pattern* (rather than a new geom) see `vignette("developing-patterns", package = "ggpattern")`.

## `with_pattern()`: a pattern layer from a layer

`with_pattern()` (re-exported from `{gridpattern}`) takes a layer
and pattern aesthetics set to constants (in `...`) or mapped (in `mapping`):

```{r with-pattern}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  with_pattern(geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x),
               pattern = "crosshatch", pattern_colour = "grey40")
```

If `{ggpattern}` has a pattern geom for the layer's geom (e.g. `GeomRectPattern` for `geom_rect()`) it is used,
otherwise the pattern geom is made by `make_GeomPattern()`.
Only the layer's geom is replaced so it keeps its stat, position, and other parameters.

## `make_GeomPattern()`: a pattern geom from a geom

`make_GeomPattern()` makes a pattern `Geom` from a `Geom`:
it has the geom's aesthetics plus the pattern aesthetics,
draws the geom's grob with its areas filled with patterns,
and draws the geom's legend key glyph filled with the key's pattern.
Use `ggplot2::make_constructor()` to make its `geom_*_pattern()` function:

```{r make-geom-pattern}
GeomSmoothPattern <- make_GeomPattern(GeomSmooth)
geom_smooth_pattern <- make_constructor(GeomSmoothPattern, stat = "smooth")

ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(am), pattern = factor(am))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth_pattern(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x,
                      pattern_colour = "grey40", pattern_spacing = 0.03)
```

A `Geom` doesn't know the default `stat` and `position` of its `geom_*()` function
(they are arguments of that function) so pass them to `make_constructor()` if they aren't `"identity"`,
as with `stat = "smooth"` above.
Without the stat the layer may fail with an error about missing aesthetics the stat would have computed
e.g. `ggridges::geom_density_ridges()` needs `stat = "density_ridges"` (which computes `height`)
and `position = "points_sina"`:

```{r make-constructor-stat, eval = FALSE}
library("ggridges")
GeomDensityRidgesPattern <- make_GeomPattern(GeomDensityRidges)
geom_density_ridges_pattern <- make_constructor(GeomDensityRidgesPattern,
                                                stat = "density_ridges", position = "points_sina")
```

### Matching areas to rows: `area_by`

The pattern geom needs to know which row of the data each area of the grob was drawn for.
`area_by` says how:

* `"row"`: the geom draws an area per row in row order (e.g. `GeomRect` and `GeomHex`).
* `"group"`: the geom draws an area per group sorted by group (e.g. `GeomPolygon`)
  or its `draw_group()` method draws a single area (e.g. `GeomRibbon` and `GeomViolin`).
* `"trace"`: the geom is drawn with a different `fill` per row
  and each area gets the pattern of the row whose `fill` it was drawn with (and then its actual `fill` back).
  This works for most geoms without knowing how they draw their areas
  (e.g. one that draws its areas in a different order than its rows)
  but it draws the geom twice and needs it to draw each area with its row's (character) `fill`.
  Areas not drawn with a row's `fill` (e.g. decorations) are left alone.
* A function of the data frame returning the rows of the areas in drawing order
  (or a single row for every area).
  It is also given the draw method's other parameters (e.g. `lineend`) by name
  if it has an argument of that name (or `...`),
  since some geoms' drawing order depends on them.

By default `make_GeomPattern()` uses what it knows the `{ggplot2}` geoms need and otherwise `"trace"`,
so `area_by` is mainly for speed or for a geom that tracing can't handle.
If the geom's grob doesn't have as many areas as `area_by` gives rows
the error says which geom and `area_by` and suggests trying `area_by = "trace"`.

A grob that only makes its areas when it is drawn (e.g. in a `makeContent()` method)
is filled when it is drawn.

## Writing a pattern geom's draw methods

For full control write the pattern geom's methods yourself:

* `default_pattern_aes()` gives the default pattern aesthetics to add to the geom's `default_aes`.
  Most are `NaN` ("unset") so that each pattern's own defaults apply:
  copy them with `default_pattern_aes()` rather than writing your own values.
* `with_pattern_aes(grob, data)` fills each area of `grob` with the pattern of its row of `data`
  within a `draw_panel()` or `draw_group()` method.
* `with_pattern_key(key, data, size)` fills each area of a key glyph with the key's pattern
  within a `draw_key()` method
  (scaling it so the key's pattern looks like the plot's).

For example this is essentially how our `GeomHexPattern` is written
(the `draw_group()` method of `ggplot2::GeomHex` draws a hexagon per row, in row order):

```{r hex, eval = has_hexbin}
GeomHexPattern2 <- ggproto("GeomHexPattern2", GeomHex,
  default_aes = aes(!!!GeomHex$default_aes, !!!default_pattern_aes()),
  draw_group = function(self, data, panel_params, coord, ...) {
    grob <- ggproto_parent(GeomHex, self)$draw_group(data, panel_params, coord, ...)
    with_pattern_aes(grob, data) # one row per hexagon
  },
  draw_key = function(data, params, size) {
    with_pattern_key(draw_key_polygon(data, params, size), data, size)
  }
)

ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat, price)) +
  stat_bin_hex(aes(pattern_fill = after_stat(count) > 1000),
               geom = GeomHexPattern2, bins = 12, pattern_density = 0.3) +
  labs(pattern_fill = "count > 1000")
```

Things to watch out for:

* **Row order.** `data` must have a row per area in the order the grob draws them
  (the order of `gridpattern::area_boundaries(grob)`)
  or a single row for every area.
  E.g. `ggplot2::GeomPolygon` draws its groups' polygons sorted by `group`
  and `ggplot2::GeomPoint` only has areas for its filled shapes (`shape` 21 to 25).
  Areas that should be filled as one (e.g. the polygons of a `MULTIPOLYGON` geometry)
  can be given the same value of `pool` (with a row per unique value).
* **Areas made when drawn.** If the grob only makes its areas when it is drawn
  use `with_pattern_aes(grob, data, delay = TRUE)`.
* **Other columns.** Besides the pattern aesthetics the other columns of `data` (e.g. `fill`)
  are passed on to the pattern (for custom patterns that use them)
  except `x`, `y`, `PANEL`, and the names of `gridpattern::with_pattern()`'s own arguments.
* **Key size.** Call `with_pattern_key()` within the `draw_key()` method.
  `{ggplot2}` may enlarge a key whose glyph has no size attributes after `draw_key()` returns
  so the `size` it is given can be too small
  (e.g. `draw_key_point_pattern()` uses the larger of `size` and the point's size).

Alternatively subclass one of `{ggpattern}`'s pattern geoms (e.g. `GeomRectPattern` or `GeomPolygonPattern`)
to inherit its default aesthetics, draw methods, and legend key.
